_: Pairs that scripts/lint-twins.mjs flags as alike and that a person has looked at.
An entry is not permission to duplicate. It is a claim that the two components
are genuinely different, plus the condition under which that claim expires — so
the next reader can check the claim instead of inheriting it.
Enforcement is bidirectional. A new similar pair with no entry here FAILS the
gate: a duplicate in the library is inherited by every product that adopts it.
An entry whose pair has stopped resembling (the profile changed, or one now
renders the other) also FAILS as stale — an excuse nobody needs any more would
silently waive a real duplicate later.

Checkbox ~ Radio.separated: both wrap a native input, take the same label/size/invalid props and render the same themed box, so the markup and prop sets score alike. What differs is the arity the browser enforces, and the third state only one of them can hold: a Checkbox is answerable alone and carries `indeterminate` for the partly-selected parent of a tree, while a Radio is meaningless alone — it is one option of a set sharing a `name`, from which the platform gives arrow-key navigation and the exactly-one guarantee for free. Folding them would mean re-implementing that guarantee in application code, which is the bug this pair exists to avoid.
Checkbox ~ Radio.reopenIf: Radio grows an indeterminate state, or Checkbox starts taking a group `name` and enforcing exactly-one — at that point the difference is a prop, not a component. Also reopen if either stops using the native input, since the platform behaviour is the whole of the argument above.
